features.title: General negative concord
features.description: Nān/nāwiht and preverbal ne or a negative contraction combine to express one negation; earlier nǣfre+ne is the bounded prerequisite. Nān can be an agreeing determiner or stand alone. A negative expression is not cancelled by a second negative.
features.scope_note: Nān/nāwiht and preverbal ne or a negative contraction combine to express one negation; earlier nǣfre+ne is the bounded prerequisite. Nān can be an agreeing determiner or stand alone. A negative expression is not cancelled by a second negative.

features.title: Negative copula indicative
features.description: Use the complete twelve-position selected negative copula table in ordinary nominal/adjectival clauses; uncontracted ne plus the positive form remains a valid alternative.
features.scope_note: Use the complete twelve-position selected negative copula table in ordinary nominal/adjectival clauses; uncontracted ne plus the positive form remains a valid alternative.

features.title: Negative possession
features.description: Use all twelve prior recognition-only nabban indicative forms for ordinary negative possession; keep their supplied and recognition history.
features.scope_note: Use all twelve prior recognition-only nabban indicative forms for ordinary negative possession; keep their supplied and recognition history.

features.title: Negative volition
features.description: Use the complete contracted negative willan indicative with a taught plain infinitive for refusal/unwillingness; distinguish tense from the English wording would not.
features.scope_note: Use the complete contracted negative willan indicative with a taught plain infinitive for refusal/unwillingness; distinguish tense from the English wording would not.

features.title: Constituent negation
features.description: Nā can negate a contrasted constituent, as ic self and nā ōðer; the finite assertion need not itself be negative. Distinguish from preverbal ne and from negative concord.
features.scope_note: Nā can negate a contrasted constituent, as ic self and nā ōðer; the finite assertion need not itself be negative. Distinguish from preverbal ne and from negative concord.

features.title: Indefinite ān
features.description: Ān with a singular noun can mean a/certain, separately from cardinal one. Reuse the already productive singular strong forms; plural cardinal-one reference cells receive no new automatic production.
features.scope_note: Ān with a singular noun can mean a/certain, separately from cardinal one. Reuse the already productive singular strong forms; plural cardinal-one reference cells receive no new automatic production.

features.title: Indefinite personal reference
features.description: Hwā/hwæt can have indefinite anyone/anything reference in an appropriate condition or concession. Familiar interrogative morphology is reused; English any is not a license for unrestricted distribution.
features.scope_note: Hwā/hwæt can have indefinite anyone/anything reference in an appropriate condition or concession. Familiar interrogative morphology is reused; English any is not a license for unrestricted distribution.

features.title: Each one
features.description: Gehwā/gehwæt is singular and distributes across a recoverable group; the genitive can name that group. Retain the actual syntactic case of the distributive.
features.scope_note: Gehwā/gehwæt is singular and distributes across a recoverable group; the genitive can name that group. Retain the actual syntactic case of the distributive.

features.title: Impersonal man
features.description: Man is a defective nominative-singular subject meaning one/people in general, with a third-singular finite verb. Do not invent oblique or plural forms in this function or identify it with every use of count noun mann.
features.scope_note: Man is a defective nominative-singular subject meaning one/people in general, with a third-singular finite verb. Do not invent oblique or plural forms in this function or identify it with every use of count noun mann.

features.title: Free-choice relatives
features.description: Swā hwā swā and swā hwæt swā mean whoever/whatever. The case follows the pronoun’s function in the supported clause, and a resumptive pronoun can carry a different main-clause role. Swā hwæðer swā selects between two. Prospective or contingent examples may have subjunctive; the form alone does not mechanically impose one mood. The attracted dative construction of Cook31.12 remains explicitly supplied.

features.title: Proportional comparison
features.description: Paired swā clauses containing comparatives can correlate two changes: the greater…, the greater…. Distinguish this from equal-degree swā…swā with a positive adjective. The two clause subjects and comparative agreement remain independent.
features.scope_note: Paired swā clauses containing comparatives can correlate two changes: the greater…, the greater…. Distinguish this from equal-degree swā…swā with a positive adjective. The two clause subjects and comparative agreement remain independent.

features.title: Both…and
features.description: Ǣgðer ge…ge strengthens paired coordination: both…and. The invariant coordinator does not assign an entire unused inflected either-pronoun family.
features.scope_note: Ǣgðer ge…ge strengthens paired coordination: both…and. The invariant coordinator does not assign an entire unused inflected either-pronoun family.

features.title: Quantity and distribution
features.description: Distinguish agreeing quantitative adjectives from a genitive specifying the whole group. In ǣlc his pęning, each distributes a singular share across plural people; the finite verb may agree with the explicit plural subject. Personal uncer can specify of us two after ān.

features.title: Preference comparison
features.description: Swīðor…ðonne compares the degree of preference between two objects or actions. In loving darkness rather than light, both compared noun phrases have the accusative role belonging to love; do not impose Unit3’s nominative copular standard.

features.title: Argument through questions and prayer
features.description: Recognize the supported reading’s rhetorical questions, grounds for action, repeated requests, and differences between an asserted statement, a prayer, and a prospective purpose. This is scaffolded source analysis, not unrestricted composition.

rules.statement: Ne precedes a finite verb. The selected negative copula combines uncontracted ne eom/ne eart/ne sindon with nis and the contracted preterite næs/nǣre/nǣron. These alternatives form one complete twelve-position indicative construction table. An uncontracted cell contains two existing words, not a new multiword inflected verb. Negative willan selects Cook’s e-vowel alternatives nelle/nelt/nele/nellað and nolde/noldest/noldon. Other spellings are valid source variants, not extra selected recall targets.

Cook’s habban table and ne+h contraction (§29), with the already checked Unit2 negative cells, give næbbe, næfst, næfð, nabbað; preterite næfde, næfdest, næfde, næfdon. The negative cells are rule-derived, not separately printed in a full negative table. Do not conflate first-singular bb with other singular f. Retain the earlier form identities and recognition histories.

Nān follows strong long-stem adjective NGDA endings, with nominative/accusative neuter plural nān and feminine plural nāna, masculine accusative singular nānne. Long ā remains. No invented weak system or general negative spelling rule.
Gehwā compounds the singular interrogative hwā/hwæt. Select prior gehwǣm (not silently substitute hwām). Accusative persons gehwone versus things gehwæt. No distinct feminine morphology or plural.
